beats.label: S1 · Korra runs to Republic City
beats.text: Seventeen-year-old Avatar Korra, master of three elements but unable to airbend, flees her White Lotus compound for Republic City to train under Tenzin, Aang's son.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes Korra's core problem — airbending block — and her arrival in the city where every following event happens.

beats.label: S1 · Amon reveals his power
beats.text: At an anti-bender Equalist rally, the masked leader Amon permanently strips gangsters of their bending, a power no one thought possible outside the Avatar.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the season's antagonist and the threat that reframes every bender's stakes.

beats.label: S1 · The duel that breaks her
beats.text: Korra challenges Amon alone and is captured. He spares her bending to avoid making a martyr, but the encounter leaves her genuinely terrified for the first time in her life.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First crack in Korra's confidence — the psychological weight she carries through the rest of the season.

beats.label: S1 · Hiroshi Sato exposed
beats.text: Industrialist Hiroshi Sato is revealed as the Equalists' weapons supplier, arming them with mecha-tanks. His daughter Asami sides against him and joins Korra's group on Air Temple Island.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Turns the Equalists from a movement into a military force and locks in the friend group.

beats.label: S1 · Tarrlok's secret
beats.text: Councilman Tarrlok abducts Korra and reveals himself as a bloodbender and the son of the criminal Yakone. Amon soon finds him and takes his bending too.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the family reveal that ends the season and shows Amon turning on his own allies.

beats.label: S1 · Republic City falls
beats.text: Equalist airships bomb the city and capture the council. Lin Beifong is stripped of her bending shielding Tenzin's family; General Iroh's relief fleet is destroyed on arrival.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The city is lost — the state Korra must reverse in the finale, and the scale of Amon's win.

beats.label: S1 · Amon unmasked, Korra restored
beats.text: Korra exposes Amon as Tarrlok's waterbending brother Noatak and airbends for the first time. He strips her other three elements, but Aang's spirit restores her and unlocks the Avatar State.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Resolves the season's villain and Korra's airbending block, but leaves her spiritual connection newly opened.

cliffhanger.text: Amon is dead, the Equalist uprising broken, and Korra is a fully realised Avatar for the first time — airbending mastered, bending restored, Aang's spirit having reached her directly. She has her power back, but she has never lived as the Avatar the world expects her to be.
questions: Now that she can contact Aang, what will Korra do with a spiritual connection she has never used?
With Mako choosing Korra over Asami, where does that leave the group's friendships?
Who steps into the power vacuum in Republic City with the council gone and Lin Beifong's force gutted?

characters.name: Korra
characters.line: The seventeen-year-old Avatar from the Southern Water Tribe, headstrong and physical, now able to bend all four elements after Aang restored what Amon took.

characters.name: Tenzin
characters.line: Aang and Katara's son, the only airbending master and Korra's mentor, a councilman and father of four young airbending children.

characters.name: Mako
characters.line: Firebending pro-bender, orphaned older brother to Bolin, ended the season with Korra after breaking things off with Asami.

characters.name: Bolin
characters.line: Earthbending pro-bender and Mako's easygoing younger brother, part of Korra's inner circle.

characters.name: Asami Sato
characters.line: Non-bender heiress and skilled driver who turned on her Equalist father Hiroshi; recently displaced from her home and dumped by Mako.

characters.name: Lin Beifong
characters.line: Toph's daughter and former metalbending police chief, stripped of her bending by Amon while protecting Tenzin's family — bending later restored by Korra.

characters.name: Amon / Noatak
characters.line: The Equalist leader, revealed as Tarrlok's waterbending brother; presumed dead after Tarrlok blew up their escape boat.

characters.name: Hiroshi Sato
characters.line: Asami's father and the industrialist who armed the Equalists with mecha-tanks and airships; defeated and captured in the finale.

beats.label: S2 · Uncle Unalaq
beats.text: Six months after Amon, a dark spirit attacks the Southern Water Tribe and only Korra's uncle Unalaq can calm it. She takes him as her new spiritual mentor, rebuffing Tenzin.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the season's antagonist as Korra's trusted teacher — the wrong choice that drives everything.

beats.label: S2 · Civil war
beats.text: Unalaq occupies the South to force reunification, then frames Korra's father Tonraq for treason. Korra frees him and pledges to raise outside armies against her uncle.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the war, Tonraq's rebel status, and Korra committing to fight her own uncle.

beats.label: S2 · Varrick's plot
beats.text: Southern tycoon Varrick bankrolls the rebellion, seizes Future Industries from Asami, and stages bombings in Republic City, framing Mako before Bolin exposes him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Varrick survives the season as a wild card; Asami loses her company; Mako and Bolin's arc runs through this.

beats.label: S2 · The first Avatar
beats.text: Amnesiac after a spirit attack, Korra relives the life of Wan, the first Avatar, who fused with the light spirit Raava to seal the dark spirit Vaatu ten thousand years ago.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up Raava, Vaatu, and Harmonic Convergence — the entire endgame is unintelligible without this.

beats.label: S2 · Portals open
beats.text: Guided into the spirit world by Tenzin's daughter Jinora, Korra is tricked into opening the northern spirit portal. Unalaq is revealed as Vaatu's ally and Jinora is trapped there.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Both portals are now open, Unalaq's true plan is exposed, and Jinora's spirit-world talent becomes central.

beats.label: S2 · Dark Avatar
beats.text: At Harmonic Convergence, Unalaq merges with Vaatu to become the Dark Avatar, tears Raava out of Korra, and severs her connection to every past Avatar.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The loss of the past lives is permanent and shapes everything about who Korra is going forward.

beats.label: S2 · A new age
beats.text: Korra reforms with Raava and destroys Unalaq, but chooses to leave the spirit portals open so humans and spirits can share the world. She and Mako quietly break up.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The world Korra hands to season 3 — spirits loose, past lives gone, Mako single — is set by these two decisions.

cliffhanger.text: Korra has defeated Unalaq but severed the Avatar's link to every past life, and has deliberately left the spirit portals open so spirits now roam the human world freely.
questions: What happens to a world where spirits and humans share the same physical realm?
Can Korra still be a complete Avatar without the counsel of her past lives?
How will nations react to a newly independent Southern Water Tribe and a spirit-touched Republic City?

characters.name: Korra
characters.line: The Avatar, newly reformed with Raava but cut off from every past life, and now the architect of an open spirit world.

characters.name: Unalaq
characters.line: Korra's uncle and chief of the Northern Water Tribe; the season's villain, killed after merging with Vaatu as the Dark Avatar.

characters.name: Tenzin
characters.line: Korra's airbending master, sidelined for much of the season but reconciled with her, and father of the spiritually gifted Jinora.

characters.name: Jinora
characters.line: Tenzin's eldest daughter, a young airbender whose unusual bond with the spirits proved decisive in defeating Vaatu.

characters.name: Mako
characters.line: Republic City cop and Korra's boyfriend at the start of the season; the two have amicably broken up by its end.

characters.name: Bolin
characters.line: Mako's brother, briefly a propaganda movie star for Varrick, now the one who saw through him.

characters.name: Asami Sato
characters.line: Korra's friend and Future Industries heir, who lost controlling interest in the company to Varrick during the war.

characters.name: Varrick
characters.line: Eccentric Southern tycoon who bankrolled the rebellion and orchestrated bombings and thefts; escaped from prison in the finale.

characters.name: Tonraq
characters.line: Korra's father and leader of the Southern rebellion, revealed as the rightful heir Unalaq displaced in the Northern Tribe.

beats.label: S3 · Airbenders Return
beats.text: After Harmonic Convergence, people across the world spontaneously develop airbending. Tenzin and Korra set out to recruit them and rebuild the Air Nation.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the season's mission and why a new Air Nation exists going forward.

beats.label: S3 · Zaheer Escapes
beats.text: Zaheer, gifted airbending by the same event, breaks out of prison and frees his Red Lotus allies Ghazan, Ming-Hua, and combustion-bender P'Li.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the season's antagonists and the threat driving every subsequent beat.

beats.label: S3 · Zaofu Discovered
beats.text: In the metal city of Zaofu, Korra meets Suyin Beifong and her airbender daughter Opal, and begins learning metalbending while Lin reconciles with her estranged half-sister.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Suyin, Opal, and Zaofu — all central to what follows this season and beyond.

beats.label: S3 · Red Lotus Revealed
beats.text: Tracking a traitor to the Misty Palms Oasis, Korra learns the Red Lotus want to overthrow every government and believe chaos is the world's natural state.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The ideology, not just the threat — needed to make sense of what Zaheer does next.

beats.label: S3 · Queen Dies
beats.text: Zaheer asphyxiates the Earth Queen with airbending and declares Ba Sing Se belongs to the people. The city collapses into looting, fire, and open revolution.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The Earth Kingdom power vacuum is the setup the next season is built on.

beats.label: S3 · Poisoned Avatar
beats.text: Zaheer takes Korra and poisons her with mercury to trigger the Avatar State and end the cycle forever. Suyin extracts the poison, but Korra is left broken in a wheelchair.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Korra's physical and psychological ruin is the state she begins the next season in.

beats.label: S3 · New Air Nation
beats.text: Jinora is anointed an airbending master, and Tenzin rededicates the Air Nomads to a wandering life of service in Korra's absence.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains why the Air Nation is a mobile peacekeeping force when the story resumes.

cliffhanger.text: The Red Lotus is defeated but the Earth Queen is dead, Ba Sing Se has fallen to revolution, and Korra sits in a wheelchair, poisoned and hollowed out, while the reborn Air Nation flies off to fill the void she can no longer fill.
questions: Who fills the power vacuum left by the Earth Queen's death?
Can Korra recover from the mercury poisoning, physically or otherwise?
What becomes of the new Air Nation now that it wanders the world in her place?

characters.name: Korra
characters.line: The Avatar, physically broken and traumatised after being poisoned by the Red Lotus, now confined to a wheelchair.

characters.name: Zaheer
characters.line: Captured leader of the Red Lotus, an airbending anarchist who killed the Earth Queen before being pulled from the sky.

characters.name: Tenzin
characters.line: Airbending master who has rededicated the reborn Air Nation to a nomadic life of service across the world.

characters.name: Jinora
characters.line: Tenzin's daughter, newly anointed as an airbending master after leading the airbenders to save Korra.

characters.name: Suyin Beifong
characters.line: Matriarch of Zaofu, Lin's half-sister and Toph's daughter, who killed P'Li and extracted the poison keeping Korra alive.

characters.name: Opal
characters.line: Suyin's daughter, a new airbender now training with the reborn Air Nation and close to Bolin.

characters.name: Lin Beifong
characters.line: Republic City police chief, reconciled with her sister Suyin after decades of estrangement.

characters.name: Mako and Bolin
characters.line: Brothers on Team Avatar; Bolin discovered he can lavabend during the fight to save the airbenders.

characters.name: Asami Sato
characters.line: Korra's closest non-bender ally, who stayed with her through the capture and the aftermath.
